chunking: fixed_size (character windows cut at whitespace; never crosses a page)
hypothesis: Baseline. Cuts ignore paragraph and sentence boundaries, so evidence sentences may be split across two chunks and each chunk carries less context; expect the lowest Evidence Hit@3 and Hit@1 of the three.
notes: Hypothesis written 2026-11-13 BEFORE any retrieval run. 1091 chunks. Test misses t04/t05 (Hit@3). Dev misses d03/d04/d11: right unit retrieved but the evidence quote is cut across two chunks (checked on d03 and d11).

chunking: by_paragraph (paragraphs packed under 1000 chars; oversized paragraphs split at sentences with 1-sentence overlap; short pieces merged)
hypothesis: Changing ONLY the chunking (A->B). Whole paragraphs keep an argument together, so I expect higher Evidence Hit@3 and better coherence than A; Hit@1 may not improve because larger chunks are less specific.
notes: Hypothesis written 2026-11-13 BEFORE any retrieval run. 703 chunks. CHOSEN by the student (frozen before test). Dev miss d07: a different chunk of the same unit was ranked above the chunk holding the evidence (a ranking miss, not a split).

filter: author filter applied in SQL before ranking ONLY when the question supplies one (4 of 20 questions; 3 in dev); other questions run unfiltered
hypothesis: Changing ONLY the filter (B->C). The filter cannot hurt questions that have no filter (identical to B); on the 4 filtered questions it removes other authors' chunks that compete for the top ranks, so it can only keep or improve Hit@1/Hit@3 on those, but the sample is too small to claim an effect.
notes: Hypothesis written 2026-11-13 BEFORE any retrieval run. Queries B's stored chunks. Test: identical to B on every question (t04 top-3 was already all Jay in B). Dev: identical to B on every question; the filter only changed the top-3 composition of d10 (a Madison chunk replaced by a Hamilton chunk) without changing hits.
